newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Ciampi reassures EU about Stet plan.
newsitem.headline: Ciampi reassures EU about Stet plan.

text.p: Italian Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi told the European Commission on Monday that a plan to transfer telecommunications firm Stet to the Treasury was not changed despite an adverse parliamentary vote.

"Ciampi repeated that the parliamentary vote has not changed anything regarding (the plan's) substance," a Commission spokesman said after a meeting between Ciampi and European Competition Comissioner Karel Van Miert.

The spokesman said the vote by the lower house on Thursday was lost on tax aspects and other minor issues. The transfer of Stet from state industrial holding IRI, its current owner, to the Treasury prior to its sale was still on track, he added.
Stet sale has been made necessary by a 1992 agreement between the Commision and Italy to reduce IRI's huge debt in return for allowing state subsidies to IRI and its subsidiaries.

The agreement, which was re-negotiated in December, obliges IRI to cut its debt by 19 trillion lire by the end of June by selling Stet, motorway operating company Autostrade, publishing company Seat and shipping firm Finmare. -- Brussels newsroom 322 2876841
